clusters.pick_reason: #2692 settles outstanding requests with a spec-conformant JSON-RPC error (-32000 'Connection closed') rather than #2600's raw HTTP 404 'Session not found', which is semantically wrong here (the session isn't missing, the transport just closed) and isn't a JSON-RPC error object. #2692 also explicitly groups outstanding request ids by their shared stream for batched POSTs and reuses any id that already has a real response instead of overwriting it, whereas #2600's settlement path doesn't describe that check and risks clobbering a completed response in a batch. #2600 does additionally clear the dangling _requestToStreamMapping correlation (a separate leak: a send() suspended in storeEvent() across close() resolves against a retired correlation) which #2692 does not mention fixing — that piece should be ported into #2692 before #2600 is closed.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #1998: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: the StreamableHTTPClientTransport SSE reader (`reader.getReader()`) is never released when the read loop exits, leaking the reader-tied stream buffer (~50MB per long-lived client) because the lock on the underlying ReadableStream is never released via `reader.releaseLock()`. Both wrap the identical `while (true) { reader.read() }` loop at streamableHttp.ts:328 in a try block to ensure the lock is released.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 replaces the ad-hoc string check with a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` helper that does spec-correct media-range parsing: it splits on ';' to strip parameters, honors the q=0 'not acceptable' quality directive, and matches type/subtype (including wildcards) rather than doing a raw substring test. #2046's fix keeps the `.includes('application/json')` substring approach, which is more prone to false positives (e.g. matching a subtype string that merely contains 'application/json' as a substring, or ignoring q=0 exclusions) and doesn't factor the check into a reusable function. Both touch the same validation block, so only one can land without a merge conflict.

members.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
members.author: Genmin
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejected requests whose Accept header listed only 'application/json' — the server required both 'application/json' AND 'text/event-stream' to be present, returning a 406 error even in JSON-only response mode. Both PRs relax this Accept-header validation for the same code path (the request-validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts) and both ship a changeset framed almost identically ('allow JSON response mode to accept application/json-only Accept headers'). clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the identical lines in buildWellKnownPath and will merge-conflict. #2215 extracts the fix into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper and additionally corrects shouldAttemptFallback's root-path check from `pathname === '/'` to `pathname === ''` — the existing strip logic already reduced a root pathname to an empty string, so the old `'/'` comparison never matched and root-path requests always fell through to a redundant fallback discovery attempt. #2214 (labeled chore) only fixes the narrower multiple-trailing-slash case, applying the same replace(/\/+$/, '') pattern in both buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls, but does not update the shouldAttemptFallback comparison, so the redundant-fallback behavior remains after #2214 alone. #2214's second call site (buildDiscoveryUrls) isn't touched by #2215's diff and should be reapplied on top of #2215 if not already covered elsewhere.

clusters.pick_reason: #2692 settles outstanding requests with a spec-conformant JSON-RPC error (-32000 'Connection closed') rather than #2600's raw HTTP 404 'Session not found', which is semantically wrong here (the session isn't missing, the transport just closed) and isn't a JSON-RPC error object. #2692 also explicitly groups outstanding request ids by their shared stream for batched POSTs and reuses any id that already has a real response instead of overwriting it, whereas #2600's settlement path doesn't describe that check and risks clobbering a completed response in a batch. #2600 does additionally clear the dangling _requestToStreamMapping correlation (a separate leak: a send() suspended in storeEvent() across close() resolves against a retired correlation) which #2692 does not mention fixing — that piece should be ported into #2692 before #2600 is closed.
